text: 开始写 CPP  !  为此我要在老电脑上重装 Windows (为了用那个传说中的宇宙IDE), 擦掉之前工作时用了两年的系统. 之前我以为我会用 Linux 用到天荒地老, 但是现在似乎已经不再有继续使用它的需求. 我连快捷键都只熟悉 MacOS 那一套了. 也开始有点嫌弃这个系统在前端方面带给我的开发体验, 不丝滑的动效让人觉得页面水平都下降了 😿 可能我不会再回到这个 "坑". 也没有探索这那的热情了. The only constant is change 😿  拜拜

现在常去的 Jewel Osco 有一个超级好的黑人小姐姐，头发紧紧地束在后面露出光泽的额头，看着很有精气神。每次我去 pick up 她都笑盈盈地帮我装货，帮我把重的东西装在书包下面，一层一层理好，装好之后会很温暖、真挚地对我说 have a nice day 。不是那种机械麻木的祝愿。其实 pick up 是给车服务的，但是我不开车所以我都会选 “can't find the spot” 然后在里面写 “Hi I don't drive, I would be at the customer service” 久而久之下来她记得我我也记得她了。真的好舍不得她呀 ╥﹏╥

愈发觉得这个带公园窗景的房间会成为我接下来生活一个恒久的梦。被大风吹得怀疑人生疑惑我为什么要来这的时候，在厨房机械地切肉分肉的时候，日常走神发呆的时候，我都会想起这个房间，想起我是如此的渴望住进去装点我的生活。它冥冥之中成为我每一个行动的注脚，直到有一天，我住够了许多漂亮房子，无论什么海景房山景房湖景房通通体验一遍，然后云淡风轻地对二十五岁的自己说也不过如此。这样想着，好像没能顺利地住进这个心仪的房间也算好事一桩。

text:
可以拿去写小学的“给予我温暖的陌生人” 六百字作文

Yesterday was such a beautiful day. I went to look at a room that directly faced a park, with the city skyline visible from the park. Looking out the window, there was a tree, and I could see residents playing in the park. Perhaps because the weather was so nice, I immediately felt this was my dream room, even though it was small, only big enough for a twin-size bed and a small table. Right then and there, I asked the roommate showing me the place if I could put down a deposit to reserve it, but he said it wasn’t possible and that he needed to consult with another roommate.

After a nerve-wracking morning, I had already started imagining how I would decorate the room after moving in. This afternoon, I received a message saying they had chosen another candidate. If I hadn’t seen the room, I wouldn’t have felt so devastated. This feeling of not being chosen is terrible. I cried for almost an hour on the spot. Recently, house hunting has been exhausting, with the rental market full of various scams (many with tactics like paying to check credit score before even viewing the place).

After composing myself, I mustered up the courage and went downstairs to go home and take a hot shower. As I passed the security room, the guard sitting inside said to me: “good night.” I was wearing headphones and still immersed in my sadness, looking at him with confusion. He repeated: “good night.” In that instant, all my sadness came rushing back. Even though I had just managed to control my breathing to avoid crying on the bus. I whispered a choked “Thank you,” afraid that I might start crying uncontrollably again, unsure if he even heard me. Then I pushed the door and left the building.

After walking for a while, I felt this wasn’t right. I stopped on the roadside, took a deep breath to calm myself, and went back. I walked up to the guard, with a voice still trembling from tears, and said: “I just came to say, sorry I was in bad emotion just now and I want to say thank you.” Then I finally left. Perhaps he didn’t know how much warmth and strength that “good night” had given me.

Something I’ve come to realize over the past year:

Once I found my own sense of agency, I stopped feeling the need to put myself down or puff myself up, and somehow, I started doing pretty well in most things I took on. Even if not amazing, at least decent—never a total disaster. I think it’s because the ability to learn is always there. If others can do it, then even without talent, I can make up for it with time and effort.

But when I didn’t have that sense of agency, my mind was a mess of I can’t do this, I don’t know that, I’m screwed, what will people think of me? With all my energy drained by these thoughts, how could I possibly get anything right?

---

可能是最近一年逐渐感受到的事实：

找到自己的主体性后，不卑不亢，不管做什么事情都能干得挺好！即使不是 “挺好” 也基本上还不错，不会完全搞砸。我想原因在于：人的学习能力就在那儿。别人能做的事情自己即使没有天分，多花一些时间也可以勤能补拙。而对于没有主体性的自己，满脑子都是在想我这个不行啊那个不会啊，好害怕完蛋了别人会怎么看我。所有的心神消耗在这上面，能把事情做好才怪呢。
